newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran urges Afghan groups to cooperate.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges Afghan groups to cooperate.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Saturday urged groups in Afghanistan to share power and avoid outside interference in the country's affairs after the Taleban Islamic militia took over Kabul.
"No (Afghan) group could push out the other groups...All should learn to live side-by-side," Velayati told Iranian Television in a satelite link-up from New York.
He did not name any specific group but was responding to a question on developments in Afghanistan, where the Taleban on Friday ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani and his forces from Kabul.
"Afghanistan's problem has no military solution. One more time we ask (Afghan) groups to sit together and solve their problems without outside interference," Velayati said.

Shi'ite Iran had supported the ousted Kabul government and was hostile to the Sunni fundamentalist Taleban, which the Iranian media have accused of being manipulated by Pakistan and the United States.
But Iran's media appear to have toned down their criticism of the Taleban in the past few weeks and Iranian officials have held talks with representatives of the Islamic militia.
